summary: Dedicated pool: sudden per-tenant throughput collapse tied to uneven slot-hogging and autoscaler lag
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-05T09:05 and 2026-03-05T11:40 UTC a dedicated GPU pool serving Lexium Health experienced repeated, short-lived throughput collapses (per-tenant P50 latency spiking to 2.5s from baseline 400ms and 5xx rate rising to ~4%). Impact: Customer-facing product endpoints backed by the dedicated pool observed degraded response times and increased client retries. Customer reported elevated error rates and user-visible latency. Environment: Dedicated capacity cluster 'dedicated-usw2-lexium-01', prod, region us-west-2; pool configured with 8x A40-equivalent slots, autoscaler policy: target_util 0.85, scale_cooldown 120s, max_burst 2. Steps to reproduce: 1) Load test with a mix of small chat (seq_len 256) and long-context generation (seq_len 2048) concurrently from two tenants and a synthetic high QPS tenant; 2) Observe scheduler allocation skew where one tenant's long sequences retain GPU slots for extended durations; 3) Watch autoscaler decisions lag behind demand shifts for ~90-180s. Observed logs and metrics: - Serving-runtime traces show long-running kernel occupancy for the long-context tenant (logs: /logs/serving/dedicated-usw2-lexium-01/2026-03-05-09) - Scheduler metrics: slot_holding_time P95 jumped to 28s (baseline 3s) - Autoscaler events: scale_down avoided due to perceived sustained utilization but scale_up delayed due to cooldown and burst limits (dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/cluster/dedicated-usw2-lexium-01) - Kernel queuing: per-GPU queue length spiked, contention on nvlink observed in telemetry. Initial hypothesis: Uneven request mix (large-context tenant + bursty tenant) caused prolonged slot occupancy, which reduced effective concurrency for other tenants. The autoscaler cooldown and conservative burst policy prevented quick capacity adjustments. This looked like GPU starvation for some tenants rather than a hardware failure. Contact/Customer reproduction notes: Lexium provided replay trace and said issue surfaced during their morning batch of long-context inference followed by a spike in interactive requests.
comments: 2026-03-05T09:28 - Talia Morgan (Support): Acknowledged with Lexium (case opened). Assigned to SRE. Initial triage indicates per-GPU queueing and long slot hold times.

2026-03-05T10:12 - Ravi Deshpande (SRE): Collected scheduler and autoscaler traces. Noticed slot_holding_time P95 jump. Posting preliminary graphs in #support-dedicated (slack thread: https://slack.redwood/archives/C01234/support-dedicated/p16234).

2026-03-05T11:05 - Ravi Deshpande (SRE): Triggered temporary config change: reduced autoscaler scale_cooldown to 30s and increased max_burst to 4 for the pool to allow faster reaction. Observed partial recovery after ~60s.

2026-03-05T13:40 - Engineering (Serving Runtime): Identified inefficient batching for long-context workload that kept GPU RT loops occupied longer than expected; opened PR redwood/serving-runtime#1482 to change batching time-slicing for long sequences.
2026-03-06T09:15 - Customer (Lexium Health): Confirmed reduction in user-visible errors after the temp config change; reported one remaining spike during a scheduled nightly job run.
investigation_notes: SRE collected pprof and perf samples on contested GPUs; tail-latency correlated with GPU kernel run-time rather than I/O stalls.
Scheduler logic allowed a single tenant to hold pre-allocated execution slots while KV cache warmup for long sequences completed, preventing other tenants from using the same GPU slice.
Autoscaler behavior: policy combined utilization across all slots; sustained utilization from the long-sequence tenant masked the need for additional slots for short-request tenants.
Experiment: Increased per-tenant concurrency weight and enforced per-tenant slot caps in a staging replica; this eliminated starvation in synthetic replay within staging cluster.
resolution: Short-term mitigation: lowered autoscaler scale_cooldown from 120s -> 30s and increased max_burst 2 -> 4 for dedicated-usw2-lexium-01; rolled change at 2026-03-05T10:15 UTC. Also applied a hotfix to scheduler to enforce soft per-tenant slot caps (config flag enabled) to prevent excessive slot holding by long-context requests. Medium-term fix: merged serving-runtime PR (#1482) to time-slice batching for long sequences and added autoscaler logic change to incorporate per-tenant request skew into scale decisions (PR redwood/autoscaler#392). Deployed to staging 2026-03-06, promoted to prod 2026-03-07 during maintenance window. Post-deployment: P50 latency returned to baseline and 5xx < 0.1% for Lexium. Follow-ups: add unit tests for slot-capping behavior, update runbook to include guidance for tuning autoscaler burst/cooldown for mixed-sequence workloads, and schedule a postmortem with Lexium on 2026-03-09.
